intro.data: The plain pipeline (at right) Cleans one record, then Charts it. Lift the WHOLE thing to run on a batch. You can lift each step (Batch Cleaner, then Batch Charter) or use the single pre-lifted machine (Batch Processor) — both must reach the same batch of charts. But every slot also offers an impostor that does a DIFFERENT job, and one pre-lifted machine is botched. Build a faithful lifted pipeline.
intro.alchemy: The plain process (at right) Smelts one ore, then Shapes it. Lift the WHOLE thing to run on a crate. Lift each step (Crate Smelter, then Crate Shaper) or use the single pre-lifted Crate Processor — both reach the same crate of tools. But each slot offers an impostor doing a different job, and one pre-lifted machine is botched. Build a faithful lifted process.
intro.spellcraft: The plain rite (at right) Kindles one spark, then Beacons it. Lift the WHOLE thing to run on a flock. Lift each step (Flock Kindler, then Flock Beaconer) or use the single pre-lifted Flock Processor — both reach the same flock of beacons. But each slot offers an impostor doing a different job, and one pre-lifted machine is botched. Build a faithful lifted rite.
intro.abstract: Lift the pipeline g∘f into F-world reaching F(C). Use F(f) then F(g), or the pre-lifted F(g∘f). Impostors are same-typed but wrong; one pre-lifted composite is not F(g∘f). Only faithful lifts reach the goal batch.

goal.data: Turn a batch of raw records into a batch of charts, by lifting the pipeline.
goal.alchemy: Turn a crate of ore into a crate of tools, by lifting the process.
goal.spellcraft: Turn a flock of sparks into a flock of beacons, by lifting the rite.

afterSuccess.data: You lifted the whole pipeline — either by lifting each step (Batch Cleaner then Batch Charter) or by the single Batch Processor. Both reached the same batch of charts, because a functor preserves composition: F(g∘f) = F(g)∘F(f). The impostors and the botched composite had the right types but the wrong behavior.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You lifted the whole process, by steps or by the single Crate Processor — both reached the same crate, because a functor preserves composition: F(g∘f) = F(g)∘F(f). The impostors and the botched composite had the wrong behavior.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You lifted the whole rite, by steps or by the single Flock Processor — both reached the same flock, because a functor preserves composition: F(g∘f) = F(g)∘F(f). The impostors and the botched composite had the wrong behavior.
afterSuccess.abstract: Both faithful routes reached F(C): F(g∘f) = F(g)∘F(f). A functor preserves composition, so lifting a pipeline equals composing the lifts.

reveal.summary: A functor preserves composition: F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f). Lifting a whole pipeline gives the same result as lifting each step and composing — provided every lift is faithful.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: map(g ∘ f) === map(g) ∘ map(f) — map distributes over composition.
